newsitem.title: UK: London postal services hit as strikes go ahead.
newsitem.headline: London postal services hit as strikes go ahead.

text.p: Strikes this weekend by two groups of postal workers will hit state-run Royal Mail deliveries in central London from Friday until Monday afternoon, a union official said on Thursday.
The union is seeking talks to settle the disputes, which the Royal Mail call "pointless and unjustified", but so far no negotiations have been scheduled, he said.

Some 1,000 Communication Workers Union (CWU) members at London's West End delivery office have voted to take industrial action over a number of sackings for sickness which, the union argues, breach a national agreement.

Separately, 200 CWU members working at a distribution centre in north-west London will strike on Friday over disciplinary action taken by management and their belief that a discipline code is being abused, the union said.
Both disputes will disrupt mail coming in and out of London over the weekend.

The Royal Mail said in a statement it had set up contingency plans to help minimise the disruption in central London. Royal Mail London director Ian Ferguson said the disputes were about management's right to "manage its employees to ensure they perform their jobs to the high standards expected of them."
The West End delivery office dispute would affect only three out of London's 119 postal districts, Ferguson said. But the CWU said industrial relations problems were widespread in the capital.
